pontosSemNo.title: Pontos sem nó
pontosSemNo.subtitle: Brand Identity: Pontos sem nó
pontosSemNo.description: The “Pontos sem nó” brand seeks to transport us to the space between the lines of our deepest unresolved questions that always return to our minds in some way, converting memories into recognizable feelings… (PLACEHOLDER)
pontosSemNo.intro:
The work compiled here is a study of the brand design process carried out during the Visual Identity Systems course of my undergraduate degree in Design. In this study, students were asked to use design research, data collection, analysis and selection methods, and the technical application of tests and settings of the piece produced in Illustrator (Adobe Cloud) to build their own visual identity manual. The brand I created was the idea of my own studio of musical animations, called “Pontos sem nó”.

The “Pontos sem nó” brand seeks to transport us to the space between the lines of our deepest unresolved questions, which always return to our minds in some way, converting memories into recognizable feelings. Pontos sem nó seeks to be part of the moment of identification, conveying the process of acceptance of those feelings in the form of music.

Represented through lines of tenderness and serenity with a lyrical touch that makes us take on the role of a pilgrim in other dimensions through escapism.

I divided the planning into 6 stages, shown in the panel below.

creationProcess.title: Creation process
paragraphs: Within the design process used, the start was marked by guided research, building a semantic board that could orient the project's conceptual decisions. This guided the concepts of tenderness, lyricism, escapism, serenity and pilgrim, which are later recognized in symbols, typefaces, colors and other representations that served as support to enrich the brand's conceptual repertoire, but also to select the sketches and tests most consistent with the characteristics attributed to the brand (carried out in steps 01 to 04).

Once that was done, we ran print tests to ensure the readability of the typeface and to simulate the behavior of the colors (which, from the start, were selected in CMYK) on printed media and products.

batucoTuco.title: Batuco-tuco
batucoTuco.subtitle: Batuco-tuco App
batucoTuco.description: Batuco-Tuco is a mobile application focused on the gamification of music theory and instrument practice. Its name alludes to the “batuque” and pays tribute to a Brazilian species and its sound, the tuco-tuco… (PLACEHOLDER)
batucoTuco.intro:
Batuco-tuco was born largely from the opportunity to bring playful contexts into the experience of continuous learning in music. In the Graphical Interface Design course, we were challenged to create an application following a process of requirement prioritization and project management, seeking to understand points of convergence and divergence in order to work on and deliver the application within the scope set in those early stages.

Batuco-Tuco is a mobile application focused on the gamification of music theory and instrument practice. Its name alludes to the "batuque" and pays tribute to a Brazilian species and its sound, the tuco-tuco, inspiring the playful theme and visual style of the project, which turns animals into skilled musicians.

The project was developed as a hands-on study of graphical interfaces and UX/UI. To ensure a smooth evolution with real-time visual feedback, the process involved structuring content maps, building a design system and applying user-centered methodologies.
batucoTuco.heroAlt: Hanni, Yopi, Gunter, Cybele and Pepo playing their instruments together on a lit stage.

lightbox.processAlt: Board of the process stages: 01 User profile, 02 Requirements, 03 Methods, 04 Similar apps and 05 Prototyping, with the little fox's head (Portuguese text).
lightbox.interfaceAlt: Interface board: app screens on nine phones, text about the exercises and the points system and three characters; Assets board with the shop items and their prices in points (Portuguese text).
lightbox.charactersAlt: Characters board: Yopi, drummer squirrel; Pepo, pianist bear; Hanni, violinist fox; Cybele, kalimba bunny; Gunter, bassist cat (Portuguese text).
lightbox.finalAlt: Final presentation: Batuco-tuco logo, the phrase “Your expression matters, and it is knowledge.”, “Music is knowledge.” and two phones with the app (Portuguese text).

creationProcess.title: Creation process
paragraphs: The challenge was to create a scalable design system and cohesive usability flows. To do that, the process was split into five stages, each one feeding the next: the user profile (persona, interview analysis and user stories) showed who would use the app and what they expected from it; the requirements turned those expectations into essential, desirable and performance features; the methods (requirement prioritization, value and confidence attribution matrix, content map and flowcharts) defined the scope and structure of the app; the similar products (benchmarking, rough wireframes and design system) guided the visual decisions; and prototyping gave shape to all of it (next stage).

I prioritized basic requirements, such as the practice activities, to guarantee functionality before moving on to complex band interactions. In the matrices, we realized that playing in real time with other users would hardly be feasible, since synchronization would depend on each person's network.

prototyping.title: Prototyping
paragraphs: From the low-fidelity screens to the high-fidelity prototype in Figma, the main flows of the app are built around theory exercises and a points system. The exercises the user completes earn coins to buy new items for the character that represents them in the game, such as a ribbon bow, a cap, a treble clef and a ladybug.

The characters are Yopi, the drummer squirrel; Pepo, the pianist bear cub; Hanni, the violinist fox; Cybele, the bunny on the kalimba; and Gunter, the bassist kitten. They were heavily inspired by well-known Nintendo and cozy mobile games, such as Animal Crossing and Cats and Soup, with a softer, “cozy” look and approach. In three weeks, I finished the entire interface, the assets and the animations, focusing on optimizing the prototype.

pontinhasSoltas.title: Pontinhas soltas
pontinhasSoltas.subtitle: Pontinhas soltas
pontinhasSoltas.description: Design and 3D modeling of characters around an identity of loose dots. (PLACEHOLDER)
pontinhasSoltas.intro: This work is an extension of the “Pontos sem nó” visual identity manual and brings the “Pontinhas soltas”, the imaginary characters who support the brand, into 3D. More than a project in itself, it was a way to give the little dolls volume and to understand how they would behave off the page, while staying true to the original illustrations.
pontinhasSoltas.heroAlt: Jemmy, Lac, Haggy, Nina and Ali, the Pontinhas soltas in 3D, side by side on a dark blue background with colored lights.

creationProcess.title: Creation process
paragraphs: Each character stands for one of the brand's concepts: tenderness, lyricism, escapism, serenity and pilgrim, and that guided the choice of their shape, color, species and expression. Unlike the low-poly models I usually make for VR experiences, here the dolls were modeled with more subdivisions in Blender, aiming to stay very faithful to the original images. The softer, rounder edges bring that sense of softness and, at the same time, a somewhat plastic texture. They are not rag dolls, but the idea is that their figure comforts whoever sees them, as if they were made of fabric, like plush toys.

prototyping.title: Prototyping
paragraphs: The textures were created in Figma and Illustrator from the identity's own palette (Image 2), keeping the contrasts and the gradient transitions between near-pastel colors that make the characters seem to glow or give off a soft light in the areas where the paint is lighter.

identidadeEvento15Anos.title: Event identity: 15th birthday
identidadeEvento15Anos.subtitle: Event identity: 15th birthday
identidadeEvento15Anos.description: Illustrated visual identity for a pair of twins' 15th birthday, from the save the date to the applications on the day of the event.
identidadeEvento15Anos.intro: The commission called for a visual identity for the 15th birthday party of a pair of twins. The service was planned around a delivery schedule, to keep the client quickly updated on the process and to show her how my work was expected to unfold.

creationProcess.title: Creation process
paragraphs: The process was split into defining the scope with the client, building a moodboard of visual references, defining the text content, sketching and prototyping. From the answers to my general briefing form for service requests, the production scope was set, giving the pieces the following characteristics: minimalist and elegant, delicate and organic, favoring pink, yellow and green, with flowers as the main elements. A moderate, stylized level of detail, intended for promotion in digital and print media.
images: First reference board: watercolor floral invitations, botanical stickers, yellow flowers and delicate frames.
Second reference board: paintings of gardens and landscapes with flowers in shades of green, orange and pink.

prototyping.title: Prototyping
paragraphs: The process started with the “Save the date”, which would also give structure to the invitation and the pieces that followed. But input from more people shifted the project's vision a little, adding new references and changing the complexity of the illustration. The main illustration guided the composition of further pieces, such as party favor tags, menus, cake box stickers and even the wrap of a “mini cakes” favor cart hired by the client. After testing the prints and making the necessary revisions, the material was applied to the promotion and to the printed surfaces. Every step was approved by the client.

caju.title: Caju
caju.subtitle: Caju
caju.description: Illustrated children's book “Caju in: Seed has no tooth”, created in the Graphic Production course with my classmates Ana and Thays: a story about facing your fears with a big smile.
caju.intro:
Under the assignment to create an illustrated children's book in the Graphic Production course, Caju was born as the expression of the bond between a group of older sisters (me and my project teammates). The synopsis: “Cajú lives a light and happy life by her mother's side, but after a rainy day, an unexpected change challenges our heroine to see her world from a new perspective. Cajú will show us how to face our fears with a big smile”.

It was the most fun brainstorming I've ever had in a project, and it gave me a very personal and genuine connection with my story and my teammates': our ideas talked to each other, and we felt like we were thinking of the same little story even before we decided what it would be.

creationProcess.title: Creation process
creationProcess.leadBefore: The creation process was carried out together with my classmates
creationProcess.leadAfter: . We first chose the niche of children's booklets and, to create the story, we drew mainly on illustrations that we asked the children in Ana's family to make spontaneously, letting their eyes guide what would be told. From there, we wrote the story together, coming up with ideas for the title and the message, and structured the script into a beginning, middle and end.
paragraphs: In the story, Caju sees her brother Juca, whose name shares the same syllables as hers, as a scary little monster and decides to face him with the thing that always makes her laugh: tickles. The weather follows her feelings too, from the sunny day to the rain and thunder, until the sky clears when the baby finally laughs and Caju discovers he doesn't even have teeth.

Later, we looked for references on Behance and Pinterest and put together a mood board (Image a), which guided the character sketches made by me and Thays (Image b): Caju, Juca, their mother Cajuína, portrayed as Mother Nature (hence the influence of the environment in expressing feelings), and the plush toys Mr. Frog, Manuel and Pedro, Caju's allies.

prototyping.title: Prototyping
paragraphs: One of the most fun steps was testing the colours, with illustrations printed without fill and painted with coloured pencils. Then I made thumbnails of all the pages following the girls' directions (Image 3), and Thays defined a colour palette for the characters and made the illustrations for the pages and the cover, which we split among ourselves to paint. With the pages ready, I wrote the texts, we tested typefaces (Image 4) and laid it out in InDesign, printing the dummy first and, finally, the booklet itself.

finalProject.title: Final project
paragraphs: The final project is the printed children's book “Caju in: Seed has no tooth”. On the last page, we left a space for the children's drawings, giving them back a place in the story they helped create.

Dedication: This book is dedicated to all older sisters and their toothless little siblings.
Title page: Ágatha Ferreira, Ana Francisca and Thays Letícia.
To Caju, her mother was the most beautiful tree. When she was with her, every day was sunny and the whole forest danced around her.
But one day, the sound of thunder interrupted the dance. And that was the first rain that clouded the day for the two of them.
Watching her mother leave, Caju feels enormously confused!
The taxi took her mother to a faraway place, where the thunder could not reach her.
She had never been so far from her mother...
Then she felt the rumble of thunder in her heart.
This new creature only came to make a mess.
The family was restless, as if everything were about to crack.
This little monster would not stop screaming! Her mother would not sit still...
Her mother holds the little monster, who screams: Uhêêêê!
The monster’s den looked like a maze, full of toys and strange sounds.
Illustration: the dark maze, with red eyes peeking out.
Caju felt herself swaying, confused and lost on her branch; her mother’s presence was now divided.
That was when she decided it was time to find a way out.

She called all her trusted friends to a meeting: Mr. Frog, Mr. Penguin and Manoel the Cat. Talking it over, the three reached a conclusion: the little monster would laugh on one condition, tickles would be the solution.
Illustration: Caju imagines the little monster and the family laughing together.
Caju goes back to the maze, determined to face the little monster!
Illustration: the maze, with red eyes peeking out.
Caju took a deep breath and moved toward the little monster’s cage.
Illustration: the little monster’s cage, under a cloud of thunder.
She gathered her courage, stretched out her arms to attack and...
Illustration: Caju stretches her arms toward the little monster.
That scary scream turned into laughter!
And to her surprise, that little monster was actually a toothless baby!
This funny story was passed on to the little monster, now called Juca.
Every time Caju remembers, she realizes that those two were the fruits of a smile, and nothing could get in the way.
